audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for laborers in vineyard, first/last reversal, third passion prediction, mother of Zebedee sons, cup, servant/slave greatness, ransom language, and healing of two blind men.

verses.restored: For the reign of the heavens is like a householder who went out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard.

familiar.text: For the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard.

modern.text: “For the kingdom of heaven is like a landowner who went out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard.

original.text: Ὁμοία γάρ ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδεσπότῃ ὅστις ἐξῆλθεν ἅμα πρωῒ μισθώσασθαι ἐργάτας εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: Agreeing with the workers for a denarius for the day, he sent them into his vineyard.

familiar.text: And when he had agreed with the labourers for a penny a day, he sent them into his vineyard.

modern.text: He agreed to pay them a denarius for the day and sent them into his vineyard.

original.text: ⸂συμφωνήσας δὲ⸃ μετὰ τῶν ἐργατῶν ἐκ δηναρίου τὴν ἡμέραν ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: Going out about the third hour, he saw others standing idle in the marketplace.

familiar.text: And he went out about the third hour, and saw others standing idle in the marketplace,

modern.text: About the third hour he went out and saw others standing in the marketplace doing nothing.

original.text: καὶ ἐξελθὼν περὶ τρίτην ὥραν εἶδεν ἄλλους ἑστῶτας ἐν τῇ ἀγορᾷ ἀργούς·

verses.restored: He said to them, You also go into the vineyard, and whatever is right/just I will give you.

familiar.text: And said unto them; Go ye also into the vineyard, and whatsoever is right I will give you. And they went their way.

modern.text: ‘You also go into my vineyard,’ he said, ‘and I will pay you whatever is right.’

original.text: καὶ ἐκείνοις εἶπεν· Ὑπάγετε καὶ ὑμεῖς εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα, καὶ ὃ ἐὰν ᾖ δίκαιον δώσω ὑμῖν·

verses.restored: So they went. Again going out about the sixth and ninth hour, he did similarly.

familiar.text: Again he went out about the sixth and ninth hour, and did likewise.

modern.text: So they went. He went out again about the sixth hour and the ninth hour and did the same thing.

original.text: οἱ δὲ ἀπῆλθον. ⸀πάλιν ἐξελθὼν περὶ ἕκτην καὶ ἐνάτην ὥραν ἐποίησεν ὡσαύτως.

verses.restored: About the eleventh hour he went out and found others standing, and said, Why have you stood here all day idle?

familiar.text: And about the eleventh hour he went out, and found others standing idle, and saith unto them, Why stand ye here all the day idle?

modern.text: About the eleventh hour he went out and found still others standing around. ‘Why have you been standing here all day long doing nothing?’ he asked.

original.text: περὶ δὲ τὴν ⸀ἑνδεκάτην ἐξελθὼν εὗρεν ἄλλους ⸀ἑστῶτας, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τί ὧδε ἑστήκατε ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν ἀργοί;

verses.restored: They said to him, Because no one hired us. He said, You also go into the vineyard.

familiar.text: They say unto him, Because no man hath hired us. He saith unto them, Go ye also into the vineyard; and whatsoever is right, that shall ye receive.

modern.text: ‘Because no one has hired us,’ they answered. So he told them, ‘You also go into my vineyard.’

original.text: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Ὅτι οὐδεὶς ἡμᾶς ἐμισθώσατο. λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ὑπάγετε καὶ ὑμεῖς εἰς τὸν ⸀ἀμπελῶνα.

verses.restored: When evening came, the lord of the vineyard said to his manager, Call the workers and give them the wage, beginning from the last to the first.

familiar.text: So when even was come, the lord of the vineyard saith unto his steward, Call the labourers, and give them their hire, beginning from the last unto the first.

modern.text: When evening came, the owner of the vineyard said to his foreman, ‘Call the workers and pay them their wages, starting with the last ones hired and moving on to the first.’

original.text: ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης λέγει ὁ κύριος τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος τῷ ἐπιτρόπῳ αὐτοῦ· Κάλεσον τοὺς ἐργάτας καὶ ἀπόδος ⸀αὐτοῖς τὸν μισθὸν ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τῶν ἐσχάτων ἕως τῶν πρώτων.

verses.restored: Those hired about the eleventh hour came and received a denarius each.

familiar.text: And when they came that were hired about the eleventh hour, they received every man a penny.

modern.text: The workers who were hired about the eleventh hour came and each received a denarius.

original.text: ⸂καὶ ἐλθόντες⸃ οἱ περὶ τὴν ἑνδεκάτην ὥραν ἔλαβον ἀνὰ δηνάριον.

verses.restored: When the first came, they supposed they would receive more, but they also received a denarius each.

familiar.text: But when the first came, they supposed that they should have received more; and they likewise received every man a penny.

modern.text: So when the original workers came, they assumed they would receive more. But each of them also received a denarius.

original.text: ⸂καὶ ἐλθόντες⸃ οἱ πρῶτοι ἐνόμισαν ὅτι ⸀πλεῖον λήμψονται· καὶ ἔλαβον ⸂τὸ ἀνὰ δηνάριον καὶ αὐτοί⸃.

verses.restored: Receiving it, they murmured against the householder,

familiar.text: And when they had received it, they murmured against the goodman of the house,

modern.text: On receiving their pay, they began to grumble against the landowner.

original.text: λαβόντες δὲ ἐγόγγυζον κατὰ τοῦ οἰκοδεσπότου

verses.restored: saying, These last worked one hour, and you made them equal to us who bore the burden of the day and the scorching heat.

familiar.text: Saying, These last have wrought but one hour, and thou hast made them equal unto us, which have borne the burden and heat of the day.

modern.text: ‘These men who were hired last worked only one hour,’ they said, ‘and you have made them equal to us who have borne the burden and the scorching heat of the day.’

original.text: ⸀λέγοντες· Οὗτοι οἱ ἔσχατοι μίαν ὥραν ἐποίησαν, καὶ ἴσους ⸂αὐτοὺς ἡμῖν⸃ ἐποίησας τοῖς βαστάσασι τὸ βάρος τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ τὸν καύσωνα.

verses.restored: He answered one of them, Friend, I do you no injustice. Did you not agree with me for a denarius?

familiar.text: But he answered one of them, and said, Friend, I do thee no wrong: didst not thou agree with me for a penny?

modern.text: But he answered one of them, ‘Friend, I am not being unfair to you. Did you not agree with me on one denarius?

original.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς ⸂ἑνὶ αὐτῶν εἶπεν⸃· Ἑταῖρε, οὐκ ἀδικῶ σε· οὐχὶ δηναρίου συνεφώνησάς μοι;

verses.restored: Take what is yours and go. I wish to give to this last one as also to you.

familiar.text: Take that thine is, and go thy way: I will give unto this last, even as unto thee.

modern.text: Take your pay and go. I want to give this last man the same as I gave you.

original.text: ἆρον τὸ σὸν καὶ ὕπαγε· θέλω δὲ τούτῳ τῷ ἐσχάτῳ δοῦναι ὡς καὶ σοί·

verses.restored: Is it not lawful for me to do what I wish with what is mine? Or is your eye harmful because I am good/generous?

familiar.text: Is it not lawful for me to do what I will with mine own? Is thine eye evil, because I am good?

modern.text: Do I not have the right to do as I please with what is mine? Or are you envious because I am generous?’

original.text: ⸀οὐκ ἔξεστίν μοι ⸂ὃ θέλω ποιῆσαι⸃ ἐν τοῖς ἐμοῖς; ⸀ἢ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου πονηρός ἐστιν ὅτι ἐγὼ ἀγαθός εἰμι;

verses.restored: So the last will be first, and the first last.

familiar.text: So the last shall be first, and the first last: for many be called, but few chosen.

modern.text: So the last will be first, and the first will be last.” The Third Prediction of the Passion (Mark 10:32–34; Luke 18:31–34)

original.text: οὕτως ἔσονται οἱ ἔσχατοι πρῶτοι καὶ οἱ πρῶτοι ⸀ἔσχατοι.

verses.restored: As Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, he took the twelve disciples aside privately and on the way said to them,

familiar.text: And Jesus going up to Jerusalem took the twelve disciples apart in the way, and said unto them,

modern.text: As Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, He took the twelve disciples aside and said,

original.text: ⸂Καὶ ἀναβαίνων ὁ⸃ Ἰησοῦς εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα παρέλαβεν τοὺς δώδεκα ⸀μαθητὰς κατʼ ἰδίαν, ⸂καὶ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ⸃ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς·

verses.restored: Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Humanity will be handed over to the chief priests and scribes, and they will condemn him to death.

familiar.text: Behold, we go up to Jerusalem; and the Son of man shall be betrayed unto the chief priests and unto the scribes, and they shall condemn him to death,

modern.text: “Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be delivered over to the chief priests and scribes. They will condemn Him to death

original.text: Ἰδοὺ ἀναβαίνομεν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδοθήσεται τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν καὶ γραμματεῦσιν, καὶ κατακρινοῦσιν αὐτὸν θανάτῳ,

verses.restored: They will hand him over to the nations to mock, flog, and crucify; and on the third day he will be raised.

familiar.text: And shall deliver him to the Gentiles to mock, and to scourge, and to crucify him: and the third day he shall rise again.

modern.text: and will deliver Him over to the Gentiles to be mocked and flogged and crucified. And on the third day He will be raised to life.” A Mother’s Request (Mark 10:35–45)

original.text: καὶ παραδώσουσιν αὐτὸν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν εἰς τὸ ἐμπαῖξαι καὶ μαστιγῶσαι καὶ σταυρῶσαι, καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ⸀ἐγερθήσεται.

verses.restored: Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee came to him with her sons, bowing and asking something from him.

familiar.text: Then came to him the mother of Zebedee’s children with her sons, worshipping him, and desiring a certain thing of him.

modern.text: Then the mother of Zebedee’s sons came to Jesus with her sons and knelt down to make a request of Him.

original.text: Τότε προσῆλθεν αὐτῷ ἡ μήτηρ τῶν υἱῶν Ζεβεδαίου μετὰ τῶν υἱῶν αὐτῆς προσκυνοῦσα καὶ αἰτοῦσά τι ⸀παρʼ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: He said to her, What do you want? She said, Say that these two sons of mine may sit, one at your right and one at your left, in your reign.

familiar.text: And he said unto her, What wilt thou? She saith unto him, Grant that these my two sons may sit, the one on thy right hand, and the other on the left, in thy kingdom.

modern.text: “What do you want?” He inquired. She answered, “Declare that in Your kingdom one of these two sons of mine may sit at Your right hand, and the other at Your left.”

original.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Τί θέλεις; λέγει αὐτῷ· Εἰπὲ ἵνα καθίσωσιν οὗτοι οἱ δύο υἱοί μου εἷς ἐκ δεξιῶν ⸀σου καὶ εἷς ἐξ εὐωνύμων σου ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ σου.

verses.restored: Jesus answered, You do not know what you ask. Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink? They said, We are able.

familiar.text: But Jesus answered and said, Ye know not what ye ask. Are ye able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of, and to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with? They say unto him, We are able.

modern.text: “You do not know what you are asking,” Jesus replied. “Can you drink the cup I am going to drink?” “We can,” the brothers answered.

original.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Οὐκ οἴδατε τί αἰτεῖσθε· δύνασθε πιεῖν τὸ ποτήριον ὃ ἐγὼ μέλλω ⸀πίνειν; λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Δυνάμεθα.

verses.restored: He said to them, My cup you will drink; but to sit at my right and left is not mine to give, except to those for whom it has been prepared by my Father.

familiar.text: And he saith unto them, Ye shall drink indeed of my cup, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with: but to sit on my right hand, and on my left, is not mine to give, but it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared of my Father.

modern.text: “You will indeed drink My cup,” Jesus said. “But to sit at My right or left is not Mine to grant. These seats belong to those for whom My Father has prepared them.”

original.text: ⸀λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τὸ μὲν ποτήριόν μου ⸀πίεσθε, τὸ δὲ καθίσαι ἐκ δεξιῶν μου καὶ ἐξ ⸀εὐωνύμων οὐκ ἔστιν ⸀ἐμὸν δοῦναι, ἀλλʼ οἷς ἡτοίμασται ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρός μου.

verses.restored: When the ten heard, they were indignant about the two brothers.

familiar.text: And when the ten heard it, they were moved with indignation against the two brethren.

modern.text: When the ten heard about this, they were indignant with the two brothers.

original.text: Καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ δέκα ἠγανάκτησαν περὶ τῶν δύο ἀδελφῶν.

verses.restored: Jesus called them and said, You know that the rulers of the nations lord it over them, and the great exercise authority over them.

familiar.text: But Jesus called them unto him, and said, Ye know that the princes of the Gentiles exercise dominion over them, and they that are great exercise authority upon them.

modern.text: But Jesus called them aside and said, “You know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their superiors exercise authority over them.

original.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς προσκαλεσάμενος αὐτοὺς εἶπεν· Οἴδατε ὅτι οἱ ἄρχοντες τῶν ἐθνῶν κατακυριεύουσιν αὐτῶν καὶ οἱ μεγάλοι κατεξουσιάζουσιν αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: It shall not be so among you; but whoever wishes to become great among you shall be your servant.

familiar.text: But it shall not be so among you: but whosoever will be great among you, let him be your minister;

modern.text: It shall not be this way among you. Instead, whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant,

original.text: οὐχ οὕτως ⸀ἔσται ἐν ὑμῖν· ἀλλʼ ὃς ⸀ἂν θέλῃ ἐν ὑμῖν μέγας γενέσθαι ἔσται ὑμῶν διάκονος,

verses.restored: Whoever wishes to be first among you shall be your slave,

familiar.text: And whosoever will be chief among you, let him be your servant:

modern.text: and whoever wants to be first among you must be your slave—

original.text: καὶ ὃς ⸀ἂν θέλῃ ἐν ὑμῖν εἶναι πρῶτος ⸀ἔσται ὑμῶν δοῦλος·

verses.restored: just as the Son of Humanity did not come to be served but to serve, and to give his life/soul as a ransom for many.

familiar.text: Even as the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.

modern.text: just as the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many.” The Blind Men by the Road (Mark 10:46–52; Luke 18:35–43)

original.text: ὥσπερ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἦλθεν διακονηθῆναι ἀλλὰ διακονῆσαι καὶ δοῦναι τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ λύτρον ἀντὶ πολλῶν.

verses.restored: As they were going out from Jericho, a great crowd followed him.

familiar.text: And as they departed from Jericho, a great multitude followed him.

modern.text: As they were leaving Jericho, a large crowd followed Him.

original.text: Καὶ ἐκπορευομένων αὐτῶν ἀπὸ Ἰεριχὼ ἠκολούθησεν αὐτῷ ὄχλος πολύς.

verses.restored: And look, two blind men sitting beside the way, hearing that Jesus was passing by, cried out, Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David.

familiar.text: And, behold, two blind men sitting by the way side, when they heard that Jesus passed by, cried out, saying, Have mercy on us, O Lord, thou son of David.

modern.text: And there were two blind men sitting beside the road. When they heard that Jesus was passing by, they cried out, “Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!”

original.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ δύο τυφλοὶ καθήμενοι παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν, ἀκούσαντες ὅτι Ἰησοῦς παράγει, ἔκραξαν λέγοντες· ⸂Κύριε, ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς⸃, ⸀υἱὸς Δαυίδ.

verses.restored: The crowd rebuked them so they would be silent, but they cried out even more, Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David.

familiar.text: And the multitude rebuked them, because they should hold their peace: but they cried the more, saying, Have mercy on us, O Lord, thou son of David.

modern.text: The crowd admonished them to be silent, but they cried out all the louder, “Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!”

original.text: ὁ δὲ ὄχλος ἐπετίμησεν αὐτοῖς ἵνα σιωπήσωσιν· οἱ δὲ μεῖζον ⸀ἔκραξαν λέγοντες· ⸂Κύριε, ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς⸃, ⸀υἱὸς Δαυίδ.

verses.restored: Jesus stood still, called them, and said, What do you want me to do for you?

familiar.text: And Jesus stood still, and called them, and said, What will ye that I shall do unto you?

modern.text: Jesus stopped and called them. “What do you want Me to do for you?” He asked.

original.text: καὶ στὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐφώνησεν αὐτοὺς καὶ εἶπεν· Τί θέλετε ποιήσω ὑμῖν;

verses.restored: They said to him, Lord, that our eyes may be opened.

familiar.text: They say unto him, Lord, that our eyes may be opened.

modern.text: “Lord,” they answered, “let our eyes be opened.”

original.text: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Κύριε, ἵνα ⸂ἀνοιγῶσιν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ ἡμῶν⸃.

verses.restored: Moved with compassion, Jesus touched their eyes; immediately they received sight and followed him.

familiar.text: So Jesus had compassion on them, and touched their eyes: and immediately their eyes received sight, and they followed him.

modern.text: Moved with compassion, Jesus touched their eyes, and at once they received their sight and followed Him.

original.text: σπλαγχνισθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἥψατο τῶν ⸀ὀμμάτων αὐτῶν, καὶ εὐθέως ⸀ἀνέβλεψαν καὶ ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ.
